newsitem.title: UK: SIB and Bank of England warning to lenders - paper.
newsitem.headline: SIB and Bank of England warning to lenders - paper.

text.p: The UK's top financial regulator the Security and Investments Board (SIB) and the Bank of England have issued a warning to banks and investment companies about the perils of rash lending decisions and overpaying top performers, said a report in The Times on Thursday.
The report said the joint warning was made in The Financial Stability Review, published this week.
The central bank and key regulators headed by SIB have said the banking cycle has reached a "critical point" for important strategic decisions about credit risk.
Companies were urged to maintain strong management controls.
The BoE and SIB also underlined the importance of vigilant compliance procedures, said The Times.
It warned that, although results form the banking sector so far appeared to be in good shape, "over-expansion of lending can create problems for the future."
The review also reiterates the warning about tough competition in the home loans market through expensive offers of cash banks and other incentives from lenders in a bid to capture business.
